$comment: Packaging policy (task 064, DR-24). The SHAPE the shipped Exarchos plugin
package must have, expressed as DATA so exactly one artifact states it.
Why this file exists. Before task 064 the policy lived in two places that
had no way to notice each other: the hand-written expectations inside
scripts/validate-plugin.sh, and the assertions in src/install/plugin-validation.test.ts
/ src/hooks-validation.test.ts. They diverged, and the divergence was total —
on 2026-08-07 the shell gate demanded `.mcp.json` (deleted on purpose in
2b62e1bf3), demanded a `hooks` field in plugin.json (removed on purpose in
e334a392b), demanded a `SessionEnd` hook (dropped on purpose by DR-7 task 016)
and forbade `SessionStart` (shipped on purpose per #1485). Every one of those
four is the OPPOSITE of what the green test suite asserts. The packaging was
right; the gate was measuring a package that stopped existing months earlier.
So the rule is: a change to the shipped package shape is a change to THIS
file. Both the gate (scripts/validate-plugin.mjs) and the test suite read it,
so they cannot disagree about the contract again — at worst they disagree
with the tree, which is what a gate is for.
Every entry carries `because` (why the rule holds) and, where a dated
decision produced it, `decidedIn` (the commit or issue). A rule whose reason
no longer holds should be deleted here, not worked around at a call site.

requiredFields.because: Claude Code keys plugin identity, command namespacing and MCP server scoping off this.
Marketplace pin + `metadata.compat.minBinaryVersion` reconciliation both read it; src/install/plugin-validation.test.ts pins it equal to package.json's version.
Points at commands/, the slash-command surface. Absent, the plugin registers no commands and fails silently.
Points at the rendered skills/ tree that `npm run build:skills` emits and `npm run skills:guard` pins.
Inlined here rather than in a standalone .mcp.json — see forbiddenFiles/.mcp.json. This field IS the MCP registration.

forbiddenFields.because: hooks/hooks.json sits at the well-known plugin path and Claude Code auto-loads it. Declaring it here ALSO registers it, so every hook fires twice.
forbiddenFields.decidedIn: e334a392b (`chore: fix hooks test`); pinned by src/install/plugin-validation.test.ts `expect(plugin.hooks).toBeUndefined()`

expected.name: exarchos
expected.because: The one server the plugin bundles: `exarchos mcp` over stdio.

mcpServers.exactBecause: A second bundled server would be registered on every consumer's machine without them asking for it. src/install/plugin-validation.test.ts pins the key list to exactly ['exarchos'].

requiredDirs.because: The target of plugin.json's `commands` field. A dangling pointer registers zero commands and reports no error.
The target of plugin.json's `skills` field — the RENDERED tree, not content/.

requiredFiles.because: The well-known auto-loaded plugin hook path. Absent, the SubagentStop token-attribution seam (#1525) silently stops feeding `subagent.tokens_used`.

forbiddenFiles.because: A standalone .mcp.json at the repo root is auto-detected as PROJECT config by Claude Code, so anyone working in this repo got the exarchos MCP server twice — once from the project file and once from the plugin. The config was inlined into plugin.json's `mcpServers` to remove the project-level auto-discovery path entirely.
forbiddenFiles.decidedIn: 2b62e1bf3 (`fix: inline MCP config into plugin.json, remove standalone .mcp.json`, 2026-02-20)

expected.because: The orientation on-ramp binding (#1485): tells the agent this project routes SDLC through Exarchos. Retained in the PLUGIN even though DR-7 retires the onboard-installer's copy for standalone-CLI consumers.
The token-attribution seam (#1525/#1561) — the only place per-subagent token usage can be observed. Feeds `subagent.tokens_used`.

hooks.exactBecause: The hook layer is observe-only (docs/adrs/2026-05-24-hook-layer-observe-only.md): enforcement lives in the MCP tools. An unlisted hook type is an enforcement surface arriving by the back door, so the shipped set is pinned exactly rather than as a lower bound. Adding a hook is a deliberate edit to this list.

retired.because: Retired enforcement hook — the `exarchos guard` gate. Enforcement moved into the MCP tools.
Retired enforcement hook — the `exarchos task-gate` control point.
Retired enforcement hook — the `exarchos teammate-gate` control point.
Retired enforcement hook — the `exarchos subagent-context` injection point.
Auto-resume machinery removed; `cli-commands/pre-compact.ts` was deleted with it.
The launcher is the lifecycle authority — session lifecycle is sourced from `launch.*` events, so the SessionEnd provenance observer was dropped everywhere.
retired.decidedIn: DR-7 / task 016 hook-surface shrink; pinned by src/install/plugin-validation.test.ts `expect(hookTypes).not.toContain('SessionEnd')`

forbiddenTokens.because: A build-time placeholder that never survives to a consumer's machine. Hook commands must resolve `exarchos` from PATH (or ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}); an unsubstituted placeholder makes every hook a silent no-op.
